title: Drivers and Barriers to HPV Vaccination in Young Adults Aged 18 to 26 Years in Germany: A cross-sectional study
summary: Human papillomaviruses (HPV) are widespread viruses that can lead to various diseases and certain types of cancer. Vaccination can reduce the risk of such diseases. Despite existing vaccination recommendations for individuals aged 9 to 14 and the option of catch-up vaccination up to and including the age of 17, many young adults remain unvaccinated against HPV. To date, there is only limited information available in Germany regarding young adults’ HPV and HPV vaccination awareness and their reasons for or against HPV vaccination. The aim of this study is therefore to examine HPV and HPV vaccination awareness, HPV vaccination initiation, and potential factors that encourage or discourage HPV vaccination among young adults aged 18 to 26 in Germany. To achieve this, a one-time online survey will be conducted with approximately 2,000 young adults. Participants will be asked to answer questions about their HPV and HPV vaccination awareness, their vaccination status, and possible reasons for or against HPV vaccination.
conditions: Prevention of HPV infections and HPV-related diseases

interventions.name: Young adults aged 18 to 26 years in Germany will complete a one-time online questionnaire assessing HPV and HPV vaccination awareness, HPV vaccination status, drivers and barriers to HPV vaccination, and sociodemographic characteristics.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Provided study-specific informed consent, including data protection regulation consent
Exclusion criteria:
Previous participation in another study within the past 6 months that focused on the topic of vaccination
